<system-reminder>
Available skills (invoke by exact name when its description matches the request):
agent-browser: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. Prefer agent-browser over any built-in browser automation or web tools.
cross-review: Cross review code using a subagent with a specified model. Use when the user asks to review code changes AND specifies a model to use (e.g., 'review with opus', 'use sonnet to review', 'review changes with gemini'). The key differentiator from the regular zen-review skill is that the user explicitly specifies which model should perform the review. The root agent reconstructs what changed from its own conversation history — no git commands are used.
frontend-design: Design distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces — mockups as HTML pages or working application pages. Use when the user asks to design a web page, landing page, UI mockup, dashboard, application page, or any visual HTML interface. Supports single designs, multiple variant generation, and integration with existing project frameworks.
grpc-expert: Expert guidance for gRPC/Protocol Buffers work in the operation-dbus-proto (OP-DBUS) workspace — designing plugin methods, generating .proto/service definitions, wiring the op-grpc-bridge, or fixing plugins with missing gRPC methods. Use this whenever the user mentions gRPC, proto/protobuf, plugin methods, the gRPC bridge, tonic, reflection descriptors, 'missing plugins' in the gRPC diagnostic page, or the seal/freeze/hot pipeline — even if they don't say 'gRPC' explicitly (e.g. 'the plugin isn't showing up on the diagnostic page', 'add a method to plugin X', 'regen protos').
plan: Planning agent for task breakdown and implementation planning. Use via spawn_subagent with skill='plan' when you need to explore a codebase and design an implementation approach before writing code.
research: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases and searching for code patterns. Use via spawn_subagent with skill='research' for read-only exploration tasks.
skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
zen-comprehensive-review: Orchestrate a multi-model code review: spawn 3 review subagents, merge findings. In PR mode, posts GitHub PR comments. In local mode, outputs findings directly. CRITICAL: this skill is costly, don't use it unless user explicitly requested to use it.
zen-review: Expert code reviewer. Analyze PR changes for correctness, security, performance, and quality. Returns findings as JSON. CRITICAL: this skill is costly, don't use it unless user explicitly requested to use it.
tuistory: Automates terminal user interface (TUI) testing. Use when you need to launch, interact with, test, or debug terminal applications, capture TUI snapshots, or automate terminal inputs.
install-code-review: Install and configure Factory Droid for automated code review on GitHub or GitLab. Supports single-repo setup or org/group-wide rollout across hundreds of repos. Use when a user wants to set up Droid review on their repositories.
install-triage: Scaffold a scheduled Slack triage automation, generalized to any company. Sets up a Python tool layer (run_triage.py) plus a HEARTBEAT.md agent loop that scans configured Slack channels for actionable messages, dedupes against a ticketing system (Linear or Jira), files tickets, and posts a run summary. Use when the user wants to stand up an automated triage bot.
review: Review code changes and identify high-confidence, actionable bugs. Use when the user wants to: - Review a pull request or branch diff - Find bugs, security issues, or correctness problems in code changes - Get a structured summary of review findings
simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
session-navigation: Navigate, search, and manage Droid sessions. Use when the user wants to: - List recent sessions - Search session history for specific topics or patterns - Resume a previous session - Get details about what was accomplished in a session - Find sessions by project, date, or content
pdf-document: Produce polished PDF documents (reports, invoices, resumes, letters, flyers, certificates, any "export to PDF" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PDF or a printable document.
powerpoint: Produce polished PowerPoint presentations (decks, slide shows, pitch decks, any "export to PowerPoint" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint, a slide deck, or a presentation.
excel: Produce polished Excel spreadsheets (reports, budgets, data exports, any "export to Excel" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for an Excel file, a spreadsheet, or an .xlsx deliverable.
word-document: Produce polished Word documents (reports, letters, proposals, printable docs, any .docx deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a Word document or a .docx file.
install-qa: Set up automated QA testing for this project. Performs deep codebase analysis, asks targeted questions, and generates a modular QA skill with sub-skills per app, a GitHub Actions workflow, and a report template. This is a complex, multi-phase process -- quality assurance is foundational and we take the time to get it right.
security-review: Security-focused code review using STRIDE, OWASP Top 10, OWASP LLM Top 10, and supply chain analysis. Use when: - Reviewing a PR for security vulnerabilities - Performing a security audit of code changes - Identifying injection, auth, data exposure, and other security issues - Running a full-project security audit reviewing every source file
deep-security-review: Correctness-first, depth-first security audit of a single repository. Invoked by /security-review when the user opts into "thorough" mode. Uses a heterogeneous multi-model jury (latest Opus + latest GPT + latest Gemini). A mandatory 3-pass floor (line-anchor verification, vendor prior-art, deep prior-art) runs against every Pass 0 lieutenant-seeded candidate; a conditional escalation tier (dataflow + reachability, exploit construction, adversarial red-team disprove) fires on per-finding triggers. Produces FINDINGS.md, JUDGE.md, DASHBOARD.md, severity-sorted master list, and optional PoC + evidence artifacts for that repo. Never uploads or submits anything; all outputs local.
wiki: Generate comprehensive codebase documentation for a repository. Uploads the wiki to view in the Factory app.
wiki-video-gen: Generate Factory-branded HyperFrames video overviews for repository wikis. Use when wiki generation reaches Phase 3.6, or when the user asks for a narrated repository overview video.
install-wiki: Install a CI action that automatically refreshes the Factory Wiki on each push to the default branch. Use when the user wants to set up automated wiki generation, install wiki CI, or configure wiki refresh.
browse-wiki: Search and read wiki documentation for a repository
incident: RCA runbook for alerts. Given an alert link (or prompted to provide one), identifies the alert type, verifies tooling/auth, and walks through root cause analysis using deep research. Persists learnings to incident-guidelines for future reuse.
</system-reminder>

The pattern here is dangerous—removing fields at low numbers creates a silent deserialization bug where new fields added at those same positions will interpret old wire data as the wrong type. For instance, if `bool success = 1` gets removed and someone later adds `string name = 1`, old clients sending `success=true` will have that varint decoded as a string, causing type mismatches or corrupted data.

I have insights, and the reconciliation changes the headline finding entirely. I changed nothing, this is all read-only analysis.

## The headline: `proto/` in the UI is a fork, not a mirror, and it has drifted wire-incompatibly

Your transport is binary gRPC-Web. `src/grpc/client.ts:80` even documents why: `application/grpc-web+proto`, because tonic-web rejects `+json`. So **field numbers are the only thing on the wire. Field names are irrelevant.**

Meanwhile the UI's "Phase 4" refactor deleted `bool success = 1` from response messages and let every later field shift down a slot, with **zero `reserved` statements** across all 469 protos. Your own STYLE_GUIDE mandates reserving. The backend never got that refactor: odbus still has **88 `bool success`**, 1 `bool valid`, 28 `string error`, 31 `_json` fields. The UI has 0, 0, 14, 8.

Result, 275 field-number collisions across 13 of the 14 shared protos:

<json-render>{"root":"r","elements":{"r":{"type":"Box","props":{"flexDirection":"column","gap":1},"children":["h","c"]},"h":{"type":"Heading","props":{"text":"Field-number collisions: odbus vs dashboard-ui","level":3},"children":[]},"c":{"type":"BarChart","props":{"data":[{"label":"orchestration","value":69,"color":"red"},{"label":"privacy_network","value":49,"color":"red"},{"label":"agents","value":29,"color":"yellow"},{"label":"internal_agents","value":27,"color":"yellow"},{"label":"registration","value":24,"color":"yellow"},{"label":"mail","value":21,"color":"yellow"},{"label":"operation","value":18,"color":"red"},{"label":"cognitive","value":12,"color":"yellow"},{"label":"op_cache","value":10,"color":"yellow"},{"label":"chat","value":5,"color":"green"},{"label":"adapters","value":4,"color":"green"},{"label":"mcp","value":4,"color":"green"},{"label":"registry","value":3,"color":"green"},{"label":"services","value":0,"color":"green"}],"showPercentage":false},"children":[]}}}</json-render>

`services.proto` is the only byte-identical file.

**`CallMethodResponse` is the worst case**, because it is how the UI invokes every plugin method:

| field | odbus sends | UI decodes as | wire types |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `bool success` | `google.protobuf.Value result` | varint vs length-delimited |
| 2 | `Value result` | `uint64 event_id` | length-delimited vs varint |
| 3 | `uint64 event_id` | `string event_hash` | varint vs length-delimited |

Every slot is a wire-type mismatch. Same shape in `MutateResponse`, `SetPropertyResponse`, `BatchMutateResponse`, `OvsdbTransactResponse`, `VerifyChainResponse`, `GetSchemaResponse`, `dbusCallResponse`.

There is a **second, independent** breakage class: your style guide rule 1, "use enums, never strings," applied unilaterally. In `privacy_network.proto`, `string container_type` became `ContainerType container_type` at the same field number, and `string wgcf_status` became `ComponentStatus`. String is wire type 2, enum is wire type 0. Also unreadable. RPC sets match perfectly on both sides, so this is purely message-shape drift.

## Where the UI's protos actually came from

`proto/ovsdaemon/v1/*.proto` does not exist in canonical odbus. It only survives at `odbus/lovable/proto/ovsdaemon/` and in `.consolidation-staging/docs-stale-archive/`. **You are building the OVS surface against an archived snapshot of the old lovable dashboard.** That also explains why `ovsdaemon/v1/streaming.proto` is the single worst offender for stringly-typed data: `row_json`, `previous_row_json`, `match_json`, `actions_json`, `flow_json`.

## Two backend services the UI cannot reach at all

1. **`op-xray-daemon`** exposes `RoutingService`: `AddRule`, `RemoveRule`, `ListRule`, `TestRoute`, `SubscribeRoutingStats`, `GetBalancerInfo`, `OverrideBalancerTarget`. This is precisely the rule-based / smart routing you were asking about. The UI has zero Xray protos, so it can manage the Xray *component* through `privacy_network.proto` but cannot touch a single routing rule.
2. **`zeroclaw.proto`** exposes `ZeroclawService` with `GetSchema` and **`WatchSchema`**. A streaming schema feed is exactly the primitive your generative-UI catalog wants, and the UI does not have the file.

## The generative-UI contract is built but not connected

`src/json-render/catalog/catalog.ts` is a real `defineCatalog`, and its header comment promises three things:

```
catalog.prompt()      → LLM system prompt describing the whole surface
catalog.jsonSchema()  → JSON Schema for structured-output generation
catalog.validate(spec)→ spec validation before render
```

All three appear **only in that comment**. Never called anywhere in `src/`. The catalog is serving as a plain component registry. Supporting evidence: zod is imported in exactly 2 files (the catalog and its test), there are **0 `safeParse` calls**, and **524 `as any`** outside generated code. The plugin schema path is `JSON.parse(comp.schemaJson)` with a swallowed catch returning `{}` at `src/hooks/use-event-stream.ts:307`.

So `catalog.jsonSchema()` is the thing you'd feed to `getstructuredoutput`, and `catalog.validate(spec)` is the guard `SpecPage` needs. Both already exist for free and are unwired.

## Codegen hygiene

`bun run proto:gen` emits **1,178 protoc warnings**: 872 duplicate-extension and 306 unused-import. Cause: all 437 `plugin_methods/*.proto` files each re-declare

```proto
extend google.protobuf.MethodOptions {
  string plugin_subid = 50000;
  string required_capability = 50001;
}
```

in their own package. And those extensions are used **0 times** as options. The mechanism is vestigial; `required_capability` actually arrives as ordinary data (`src/components/PluginPage.tsx:55`).

Also against your own guide: **442 of 469** packages lack the mandated `.vN` suffix, and **18 of 79** enums lack `_UNSPECIFIED = 0`.

`npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` currently fails with 6 errors, two of which are `UIMessageKind`/`UIMessageRole` enum-vs-string comparisons in `ChatWidget.tsx` and `ChatPage.tsx`, the same string-to-enum migration hazard showing up on the TS side.

## The tooling you already mirror would have caught all of it

You have `bufbuild__buf` and `bufbuild__protovalidate` in `repos-bulk`, and I just added `bufbuild__claude-plugins`. There is no `buf.yaml` anywhere, and protovalidate is imported by 0 files. `buf breaking --against` against odbus would have blocked all 275 collisions at commit time. `buf lint` covers the versioning, `_UNSPECIFIED`, and unused-import findings. The `STYLE_GUIDE.md` footer says "Enforced by: Service Design Review," which is the actual root cause: a 469-file contract enforced by human review.

## What I'd suggest, in order

1. Decide the direction of truth. Right now neither side is authoritative and both drifted. My read is odbus should own the protos and the UI should consume, not fork.
2. Make odbus the single source: one `buf.yaml` module there, UI consumes via `buf.gen.yaml` or a git submodule. Delete the UI's fork.
3. Re-derive the UI protos from odbus, then apply the Phase 4 refactor **on the odbus side** with `reserved` on every removed number, so both move together.
4. Add `buf lint` + `buf breaking` to CI. That mechanizes your whole `REFACTORING_CHECKLIST.md`.
5. Collapse the 437 duplicate extension blocks into one shared `options.proto`, or drop them since nothing reads them.
6. Wire `catalog.validate()` into `SpecPage` and `catalog.jsonSchema()` into the structured-output path.
7. Import `op-xray-daemon`'s `RoutingService` if you want routing-rule control in the console.

content.text:
You're right to push back. I overstated it, and the reason it renders is the thing I should have checked first.

## The correction

I claimed the contract drift was broadly breaking. It isn't. Sorted by message, all 9 colliding messages in `operation.proto` are on the **write/action path**:

`BatchMutateResponse`, `CallMethodResponse`, `MutateResponse`, `SetPropertyResponse`, `OvsdbTransactResponse`, `dbusCallResponse`, `DbusGetPropertyResponse`, `GetSchemaResponse`, `VerifyChainResponse`

And the messages your render path actually consumes, `ListPluginsResponse` and `GetStateResponse`, are **clean**. Identical field numbering on both sides. That is why the browser looks fine. The dashboard paints itself from list/state reads, and those decode correctly.

## Two things I got wrong about the mechanism

**1. Proto3 omits default scalars.** In `CallMethodResponse`, odbus has `bool success = 1`. When `success` is `false`, field 1 is *not on the wire at all*. So the UI's `result` at field 1 just stays undefined and you get an empty render, not a crash. A mismatch only materialises when `success == true`, i.e. only on a *successful* mutation. That is why casual browsing never trips it.

**2. Not every collision is a wire-type conflict.** I lumped them together. They fail in two different ways:

| kind | example | wire types | behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| shifted by deleted `success` | `CallMethodResponse` #2 `Value result` vs UI `uint64 event_id` | 2 vs 0 | tag mismatch, decode error or skip |
| retyped in place | `GetSchemaResponse` #1 `string schema_json` vs UI `Struct schema` | 2 vs 2 | **wire types match**, so it decodes "successfully" and silently produces garbage |

That second row is the more insidious one, and it is not a crash at all. `string` and `Struct` are both length-delimited, so protobuf-ts happily reads the JSON text bytes and tries to parse them as a `Struct`. You get an empty or nonsense schema, no error.

Same class: `string container_type` to `ContainerType` in `privacy_network.proto` is string vs enum, which *is* a real wire-type conflict (2 vs 0), so that one does break.

## What I verified vs what I inferred

Verified:
- Running binary `/usr/local/bin/op-grpc-bridge`, Aug 2 03:49, built *after* the Aug 1 21:18 proto rewrite.
- Its embedded reflection descriptor literally contains `CallMethodResponse` then `success`, `result`, `event_id`, `event_hash`, `error`. So the live server is on the new shape.
- Transport is binary `application/grpc-web+proto` (`src/grpc/client.ts:295`), so names do not matter, only numbers.
- The UI does wire up the affected calls: `callMethod`, `mutate`, `setProperty` at `src/grpc/client.ts`, plus 5 `verifyChain` and 9 `getSchema` sites.

Not verified: I could not complete a live write-path call. `127.0.0.1:8090` returned `grpc-status: 16` UNAUTHENTICATED, and I did not go looking for your credentials. So the runtime consequence on the write path is read off the descriptors, not observed.

## The honest version of the finding

The drift is real and the live server genuinely disagrees with the UI's protos, but it is **latent, not active**. It is scoped to mutations, plugin method invocation, OVSDB transact, chain verification, and schema fetch. Reads are fine, which is 100% of what you see when you load a page.

The single testable prediction: **invoke a plugin method that succeeds** and the result should come back empty or malformed rather than correct, because that is the only moment `success = true` puts a varint in field 1. If you have an Invoke page action handy, that is a 30-second check and it either confirms or kills the whole thesis.

The rest of my earlier report stands on its own evidence and is independent of this: the 1,178 protoc warnings, 437 unused extension blocks, 442 unversioned packages, and `catalog.validate`/`jsonSchema`/`prompt` existing only in a comment. Those aren't affected by the reconciliation.

content.text:
This reframes everything, and in your favour. Thank you for the correction.

## There are two consoles, and the Rust one is right

| copy | `CallMethodResponse` field 1 | how it gets the contract |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/operation.proto` | `bool success` | source of truth, Aug 1 21:18 |
| **`crates/zeroclaw-gui`** (Rust, egui) | `success` | `build.rs` reads `../op-grpc-bridge/proto/operation.proto` **directly** |
| running `op-grpc-bridge` binary | `success` (verified in embedded descriptor) | built Aug 2 03:49 from source |
| `lovable/proto/operation.proto` (archived) | `bool success` | old snapshot, still agrees |
| **`operation-dashboard-ui-07/proto/operation.proto`** | `google.protobuf.Value result` | **hand-copied**, Jul 30 |

Four out of five agree. The Vite dashboard is the sole outlier, and my earlier "reconcile in both directions" advice was wrong. There is nothing to reconcile on the odbus side.

## The structural reason, which is the actual insight

`zeroclaw-gui/build.rs`:

```rust
const OPERATION_PROTO: &str = "../op-grpc-bridge/proto/operation.proto";
...
tonic_build::configure().build_server(false).build_client(true)
    .out_dir("src/proto").compile_protos(&proto_files, &include_dirs)?;
```

The Rust console **cannot drift**. It compiles the canonical proto from the sibling crate on every `cargo build`. Its `src/proto/operation.v1.rs` is a committed build artifact, regenerated in place.

The Vite dashboard's `proto:gen` runs `protoc -I proto` against its own vendored `proto/` directory. Drift is not a mistake anyone made, it is the **guaranteed** outcome of that design. The Jul 30 Phase 4 refactor was applied to the copy, and the copy is the only thing `protoc` ever sees.

So the fix is not a proto migration. It is one line of build wiring: point the Vite app at `../odbus/crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto` the way `build.rs` does, and delete the vendored `proto/`. That also erases the 437 duplicated extension blocks and the 442 unversioned packages in one move, since those files aren't the source of truth either.

## Second finding: two schema pipelines, two catalogs

`zeroclaw-gui/Cargo.toml` pulls `schemars = "1"` (labelled "Serialization / schema-as-code") plus `prost-reflect` and `tonic-reflection`. It has `src/catalog/{dsl,interpret,static_pages,store,client}.rs` and `src/schema.rs`.

So the Rust console derives JSON Schema from Rust types via schemars, and the Vite console derives JSON Schema from zod via `defineCatalog`. Two independent generators for what is supposed to be one UI contract, and the Vite side never even calls `catalog.jsonSchema()`. That is a second, quieter fork running alongside the proto one.

The Rust side also uses `prost-reflect` + `tonic-reflection`, meaning it can discover the server's schema dynamically at runtime. That is the capability gap I flagged earlier as a "gap with no skill" for tonic reflection: you already built it, just not in the Vite app.

## Third finding: five UIs in the tree

- `operation-dashboard-ui-07` (Vite, `vite_react_shadcn_ts`, has `json-render`)
- `odbus/crates/` root, **another** Vite app with the identical package name `vite_react_shadcn_ts`, its own `src/App.tsx`, `src/api`, `src/pages`
- `odbus/crates/op-web/ui`
- `odbus/crates/zeroclaw-gui` (native Rust)
- `odbus/lovable` and `odbus/lovable/.zeroclaw` (archived, and the only place `proto/ovsdaemon/` exists)

That last point stands from before and now makes more sense: the Vite app's OVS surface came from the `lovable` archive because there was no canonical ovsdaemon proto to copy from.

## Revised bottom line

- My "275 collisions" count is accurate but I mis-assigned blame. It is one-directional drift in one of five UIs.
- My severity claim was too strong, for the reason you spotted: reads are clean, writes collide, and proto3 omits `success=false` so most paths look fine.

<skill name="grpc-expert" filePath="/home/jeremy/.agents/skills/grpc-expert/SKILL.md">
# gRPC Expert — OP-DBUS

This workspace does **not** hand-write per-plugin `.proto` files. Proto generation is
automatic, driven entirely by each plugin's `PluginSchema`. If you remember one thing
from this skill: **fixing a plugin's gRPC surface means editing its Rust schema
function, not writing `.proto`.**

## The real pipeline (roll → seal → freeze → hot)

```
1. Plugin declares  → PluginSchema { methods: HashMap<String, MethodDecl>, signals: Vec<SignalDecl>, ... }
                       in crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<plugin>.rs
2. Schema gets put   → op-projection's SchemaEngine publishes the catalog hash
                       (op_identity::schema_bridge::schema_catalog_hash())
3. Sealed by blob    → op-blob seals the plugin object into an immutable blob:
                       /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob
                       (op-blob is the ONLY writer — never write blobs elsewhere)
4. Descriptors       → TWO separate reflection layers exist, don't confuse them:
   for reflection       a) STATIC: crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs generates
                            plugin_methods.proto from every plugin's schema.methods,
                            compiles it with tonic_build into operation_descriptor.bin
                            (a protobuf FileDescriptorSet), served by tonic-reflection.
                         b) DYNAMIC: crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/dynamic_reflection.rs
                            (ActiveReflectionCatalog) hydrates live from the sealed
                            SHM blob catalog via hydrate_reflection_from_shm() —
                            this is the "frozen" descriptor set for what's actually
                            present right now, independent of what's compiled in.
5. Frozen            → the blob + its descriptors are immutable once sealed.
6. gRPC socket = hot → crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs registers the
                       generated per-plugin service (plugin_method_routes.rs,
                       add_routes()) on the tonic UDS bridge, dispatching each
                       RPC to call_generated_plugin_method_typed(plugin_id,
                       schema_name, ...) which routes through PluginService.CallMethod
                       — i.e. gRPC never bypasses D-Bus, it's a bridge, not a
                       second control plane.
```

A plugin shows green/connected on the gRPC diagnostic page **iff**:
- its `PluginSchema.methods` is non-empty (empty → `build.rs` silently skips it —
  see `collect_plugin_methods()`), **and**
- the plugin is sealed in the SHM blob catalog.

## Where to actually make changes

| Task | File |
|---|---|
| Add/fix methods for plugin `<name>` | `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs`, inside `<name>_schema()` |
| Reusable input/output builders | `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs` |
| Regenerate the derived `.proto` + routes | Just rebuild — `build.rs` regenerates on every `cargo build -p op-grpc-bridge` (it `rerun-if-changed`s `../op-plugins/src/state_plugins`) |
| Wire a genuinely new (non-plugin-derived) service | `crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/*.proto`, add to the `compile_protos` list + `rerun-if-changed` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs`, then register in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs` |
| Inspect what's currently generated | `target/{debug,release}/build/op-grpc-bridge-*/out/plugin_methods.proto` (build artifact — never hand-edit) |

**Never** create files under a `/proto/plugin_methods/` directory or a
`plugin_methods_unified.proto` by hand — those paths don't exist in this repo and
aren't part of the real pipeline; that was a stale spec from an earlier session.
The single source of truth is `schema.methods`.

## Adding methods to a plugin (the actual workflow)

Look at `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/proxy_server.rs` (`proxy_server_schema()`)
for the canonical pattern:

```rust
use op_state_store::{MethodDecl, PluginSchema, SideEffect};

schema.methods.insert(
    "start_proxy".to_string(),
    method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<StartProxyInput, plugin_scaffold_helpers::AckOutput>(
        "start_proxy",
        SideEffect::Mutation,       // Read | Mutation
        false,                       // idempotent?
        "cap.network.proxy.start@v1",   // required_capability
        "mut.network.proxy.start@v1",   // subid — must follow the taxonomy in CLAUDE.md
    ),
);
```

- Define `StartProxyInput` (and a typed output struct, or reuse `AckOutput`) as
  `#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]` structs — the JSON Schema is derived, never
  hand-written as `serde_json::json!({...})` unless there's no existing helper.
- `method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<Input, Output>` is the current
  (non-deprecated) helper; the single-generic `method_decl_from_schemars` is
  deprecated but still present for legacy callers.
- `subid` must be registered in the canonical registry per CLAUDE.md
  (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs`) — CI enforces
  uniqueness.
- For plugins with **zero** declared methods today (the ones missing from the
  diagnostic page), don't hand-author their methods one by one — see
  **The Auto-Creator Plugin** below. That's the actual deliverable: a plugin
  that finds these gaps and fills them itself, using real research per plugin.

## The Auto-Creator Plugin (an ongoing capability, not a one-off batch)

This is **not** a one-time task to fix ~11 named plugins. It's a standing
system capability: whenever the system encounters *any* missing plugin —
now, or a new one added in the future — it automatically generates that
plugin and submits it for **human review**, never auto-merges/auto-seals it
unreviewed. The current ~11 gaps are just the first real instances that
exercise this, not the scope.

Consistent with this workspace's "reactive, not polled" principle (CLAUDE.md):
this should be triggered by an actual arrival/lookup that reveals the gap
(e.g. a D-Bus/gRPC call or reflection lookup against a plugin whose
`schema.methods` is empty, or a plugin name that doesn't resolve at all),
not a cron-style sweep re-scanning all plugins on a timer.

Build it as a plugin itself (same `PluginSchema`/`MethodDecl` pattern as every
plugin in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`), whose job is to:

1. **Detect a gap on encounter** — when something references a plugin that's
   missing or has `schema.methods.is_empty()` (same emptiness check
   `build.rs::collect_plugin_methods` already uses to skip plugins), that's
   the trigger — not a periodic scan of the whole registry.
2. **Research that specific gap** — drive deep research via the **NotebookLM
   MCP** (once wired up) to determine what capabilities/operations the
   missing plugin should realistically expose, given its existing state
   struct (if any), documentation, and prior art from comparable plugins
   already in the registry. This replaces guessing or generic Get/List/Watch
   stubs with a grounded, plugin-specific proposal.
3. **Synthesize typed schemas** — turn the research output into real Rust
   input/output structs (`#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]`) and `MethodDecl`
   entries — per the "no `AckOutput`" rule above, every synthesized method
   needs its own meaningful typed request/response, not a generic ack.
4. **Submit for human review — do not auto-apply.** The output is a proposed
   plugin/schema (e.g. a diff/PR against `<name>_schema()`, or a new
   `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs` for a wholly new plugin),
   held for a human to approve before it's merged. Only after human approval
   does it enter the normal pipeline (build → proto → reflection → sealed
   blob → hot). The auto-creator must never seal a blob or register a plugin
   into the live catalog on its own. It never emits `.proto` directly and
   never writes to `/proto/plugin_methods/` — the single source of truth
   stays `schema.methods`, authored by a human-approved change.

In short: this is a **standing, reactive meta-plugin that drafts schemas for
whatever plugin is found missing, research-backed via NotebookLM, gated by
human review** — not a fixed batch job for a specific list of plugins.

## JSON Schema → proto type mapping (what `build.rs` actually does)

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs::json_schema_type_to_proto` maps:

| JSON Schema | Proto type |
|---|---|
| `string` (or has non-empty `enum`) | `string` |
| `boolean` | `bool` |
| `integer` | `int64` |
| `number` | `double` |
| `array` | `repeated <item type>` |
| `object` with `properties` | `google.protobuf.Struct` |
| anything else / untyped | `google.protobuf.Value` |

Field numbers are **not** sequential — they're an FNV-1a hash of the field name
(`stable_field_number`), deliberately stable across regenerations rather than
assignment-order-stable. This is intentional in this codebase (schemas are
generated from Rust structs whose field order can shift); don't "fix" it to
sequential numbering without checking with the user first, since wire
compatibility here depends on the hash being stable, not on classic proto
field-number discipline.

## Known project-specific tensions vs. generic gRPC best practice

Be aware of these before applying textbook advice unmodified:

- **Do not use `AckOutput { success: bool }` for new/generated methods.**
  It exists in the codebase (see `proxy_server.rs`) as a legacy shortcut for
  "no meaningful return value," but every method a plugin exposes should have
  a real, dedicated typed **input** struct and typed **output** struct that
  reflect what the operation actually consumes and returns — not a generic
  bool. This matters especially for the auto-creator (below): when it
  synthesizes methods for a previously-empty plugin, it must generate a
  specific `<Method>Input` and `<Method>Output` schemars struct per method,
  never fall back to `AckOutput`. Errors still go through `tonic::Status` /
  D-Bus error replies, never a `success: false` field.
- **Enums are flattened to `string`, not real proto `enum`.** JSON Schema
  `enum` currently maps to proto `string` (see table above), so the classic
  `FOO_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0` convention isn't applied by the generator today.
  If asked to add real proto enums, that requires changing
  `json_schema_type_to_proto` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs`, not just the
  plugin schema.
- **No streaming (`Watch`) support in the generator.** Every generated RPC is
  unary (`rpc X(Request) returns (Response)`); `stream` responses aren't
  emitted by `generate_plugin_methods_proto`. A real `Watch`/streaming RPC for
  a plugin needs a hand-written service in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/`, not
  a `MethodDecl`.
- **One generated file per bridge crate**, not the "1-1-1" file-per-message
  convention — `plugin_methods.proto` bundles every plugin's messages/services
  in one generated file. That's fine; it's a build artifact, not hand-maintained
  source, so the usual "small modular .proto files" guidance doesn't apply to it.

## Generic protobuf/gRPC conventions (still apply to hand-written `.proto`)

For any `.proto` you *do* hand-write (domain services under
`crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/`, not plugin-derived ones):

- `snake_case` field names, `CamelCase` message/service/RPC names, package names
  lowercase (this repo uses `operation.plugin.v1`-style packages).
- Reserve field numbers for removed fields; never reuse them.
- Prefer `optional` for fields that may be absent; avoid letting one field's
  value change the semantic meaning of another.
- Real proto `enum`s (where you control the generator, e.g. hand-written
  services) always start with `..._UNSPECIFIED = 0`.
- Use gRPC status codes (`tonic::Status`) for error paths; reserve response
  message fields for actual data.
- TLS is mandatory in this workspace (per CLAUDE.md zero-trust transport) —
  never wire a new gRPC service as plaintext, even over UDS.
- Server reflection (`tonic-reflection`) must stay wired for every new service
  so it's discoverable by `op-cognitive-mcp` and the gRPC diagnostic page —
  don't add a service that bypasses reflection registration.

## Quick diagnostic checklist

If a plugin isn't showing up / isn't callable over gRPC:

1. Does `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs`'s `<name>_schema()`
   actually populate `schema.methods`? (Empty → `build.rs` skips it entirely.)
2. Is the plugin registered via `inventory::submit! { PluginReg::new(...) }` in
   its own file (self-registration — check `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`
   only if the plugin doesn't show up in `available_plugins()` at all)?
3. Did `cargo build -p op-grpc-bridge` actually rerun? (`build.rs` only reruns on
   changes under `../op-plugins/src/state_plugins` or `build.rs` itself.)
4. Is the plugin actually **sealed** in the SHM blob catalog
   (`/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/`)? Static compiled-in proto support and the
   *dynamic* "hot" reflection/routing are two different gates — a plugin can
   compile fine and still be invisible if it was never sealed.

[![License](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/7c587813fae7d172853bbbde3bb080a171f1117331849bc06d1eab748613a22c/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f6769746875622f6c6963656e73652f6275666275696c642f636c617564652d706c7567696e733f636f6c6f723d626c756526763d31)](https://github.com/bufbuild/claude-plugins/blob/main/LICENSE)[![Slack](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/e019a16e3d39f7b36ad8d999a6cc7d82f3574e565b6719e84bbbdc3224f72375/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f536c61636b2d4275662d253233653031353633)](https://buf.build/links/slack)

Official [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) plugins from [Buf](https://buf.build/) for Protocol Buffers, Connect, and BSR development.

## Installation

[Permalink: Installation](https://github.com/bufbuild/claude-plugins#installation)

Add this marketplace to Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add https://github.com/bufbuild/claude-plugins
```

Install a plugin:

```
/plugin install protobuf@buf-plugins
```

## Available Plugins

[Permalink: Available Plugins](https://github.com/bufbuild/claude-plugins#available-plugins)

### protobuf

[Permalink: protobuf](https://github.com/bufbuild/claude-plugins#protobuf)

Protocol Buffers development with Buf toolchain and best practices.

- **Schema design**: Field types, enums, oneofs, maps, evolution patterns
- **Code generation**: Templates for Go (gRPC/Connect), TypeScript, Python, Java
- **Validation**: [Protovalidate](https://protovalidate.com/) constraint patterns
- **Tooling**: buf CLI, troubleshooting, migration from protoc

Triggers on: `*.proto`, `buf.yaml`, `buf.*.yaml`, `buf.gen.yaml`, `buf.gen.*.yaml`, `buf.lock`

USER: TOOL_RESULT: # gRPC Proto Style Guide

This guide documents the best practices applied to proto files in this project. Use these patterns when authoring new protos or refactoring existing ones.

## Core Principles

1. **Type Safety**: Use enums for all enumerated values, never strings
2. **Structured Data**: Use `google.protobuf.Struct` for flexible JSON, not string fields with `_json` suffix
3. **Error Handling**: Let gRPC status codes carry error semantics; remove `success` fields
4. **Consistency**: Apply the same patterns across all services
5. **Clarity**: Messages should be self-documenting; field names describe their purpose

## Proto3 Syntax

- Always use `syntax = "proto3";`
- Import well-known types when needed:
  ```proto
  import "google/protobuf/timestamp.proto";
  import "google/protobuf/struct.proto";
  import "google/protobuf/duration.proto";
  import "google/protobuf/empty.proto";
  ```

## Package Naming

- Use semantic versioning in package names: `package service.v1;`
- Use lowercase with dots: `package auth.v1;`, not `AuthV1` or `auth_v1`
- Organize sub-domains as: `package core.assistant.v1;`

## Message Design

### Naming

- Use PascalCase for message names: `CreateUserRequest`
- Use snake_case for field names: `user_id`, `created_at`, `is_active`
- Use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for enum values: `STATUS_ACTIVE`, `ROLE_ADMIN`

### Field Numbers

Reserve field numbers for deprecated fields to prevent accidental reuse:

```proto
message User {
  string user_id = 1;
  string name = 2;
  reserved 3;  // was email, removed in v1.2
  string phone = 4;
}
```

### Optional vs. Repeated

- Use `optional` for fields that may not always be present
- Use `repeated` for collections (never use `optional` with `repeated`)
- Proto3 all-scalar fields are implicitly optional (zero = absence)

### Structured Data (NOT JSON Strings)

❌ **Don't do this:**
```proto
message AnalyzeRequest {
  string arguments_json = 1;  // Anti-pattern
  string metadata_json = 2;
}
```

✅ **Do this:**
```proto
message AnalyzeRequest {
  google.protobuf.Struct arguments = 1;
  google.protobuf.Struct metadata = 2;
}
```

**Why:** Structured data is queryable, typed, and language-native. JSON strings are opaque.

### Oneof for Alternatives

Use `oneof` for mutually exclusive fields:

```proto
message Event {
  string event_id = 1;
  oneof payload {
    UserCreated user_created = 2;
    UserDeleted user_deleted = 3;
    OrderPlaced order_placed = 4;
  }
}
```

## Enums

### Naming & Values

```proto
enum OrderStatus {
  ORDER_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0;  // Always have 0 as default
  ORDER_STATUS_PENDING = 1;
  ORDER_STATUS_PROCESSING = 2;
  ORDER_STATUS_COMPLETED = 3;
  ORDER_STATUS_FAILED = 4;
}
```

**Rules:**
- Prefix all enum values with the enum name (prevents naming collisions)
- First value must always be `_UNSPECIFIED = 0` (required by proto3)
- Never reuse deleted enum values; reserve them instead:
  ```proto
  enum OrderStatus {
    ORDER_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
    ORDER_STATUS_PENDING = 1;
    reserved 2;  // was ORDER_STATUS_ARCHIVED, removed in v2.0
    ORDER_STATUS_PROCESSING = 3;
  }
  ```

### Common Enums (Place in common.proto)

Share these across services:

```proto
// Pagination styles
message Pagination {
  uint32 limit = 1;
  uint32 offset = 2;
  string cursor = 3;
}

// Common status enums
enum RunStatus {
  RUN_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  RUN_STATUS_PENDING = 1;
  RUN_STATUS_RUNNING = 2;
  RUN_STATUS_COMPLETED = 3;
  RUN_STATUS_FAILED = 4;
  RUN_STATUS_CANCELLED = 5;
}

enum EventType {
  EVENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  EVENT_TYPE_TOOL_CALL = 1;
  EVENT_TYPE_TOOL_RESULT = 2;
  EVENT_TYPE_MESSAGE = 3;
  EVENT_TYPE_STATUS = 4;
  EVENT_TYPE_ERROR = 5;
}
```

## Service Design

### RPC Method Naming

- Unary: `Create`, `Get`, `Update`, `Delete`, `List`, `Analyze`, `Search`
- Streaming: `Stream`, `Watch`, `Listen`, `Subscribe`
- Bidirectional: `Communicate`, `Session`, `Interactive`

```proto
service OrderService {
  // Unary RPCs
  rpc CreateOrder(CreateOrderRequest) returns (Order);
  rpc GetOrder(GetOrderRequest) returns (Order);
  rpc ListOrders(ListOrdersRequest) returns (ListOrdersResponse);
  
  // Server streaming
  rpc WatchOrders(WatchOrdersRequest) returns (stream OrderEvent);
  
  // Client streaming
  rpc SubmitOrderBatch(stream OrderRequest) returns (BatchResult);
  
  // Bidirectional streaming
  rpc ChatWithSupport(stream ChatMessage) returns (stream ChatMessage);
}
```

### Request/Response Naming

- `<Method><Request>` and `<Method><Response>`
- For list operations: `List<Entity>Request` and `List<Entity>Response`

```proto
// Unary
message CreateOrderRequest { ... }
message CreateOrderResponse { ... }
message Order { ... }  // Also valid as return type

// Streaming
message StreamOrderEventsRequest { ... }
// Returns: stream OrderEvent (no Response needed)

// Batch operations
message BatchCreateOrderRequest { ... }
message BatchCreateOrderResponse { ... }
```

## Error Handling

### Never Use success: bool

❌ **Don't:**
```proto
message CreateUserResponse {
  bool success = 1;
  string error = 2;
}
```

✅ **Do:**
```proto
message CreateUserResponse {
  string user_id = 1;
  string name = 2;
}
// Errors are handled by gRPC status codes:
// - OK (0): success
// - INVALID_ARGUMENT (3): bad request
// - ALREADY_EXISTS (6): duplicate user
// - INTERNAL (13): server error
```

### gRPC Status Codes

Map domain errors to standard codes:

| Scenario | Code | Example |
|----------|------|---------|
| Missing required field | `INVALID_ARGUMENT` | Empty user_id |
| Resource not found | `NOT_FOUND` | Order doesn't exist |
| Already exists | `ALREADY_EXISTS` | Email already registered |
| Permission denied | `PERMISSION_DENIED` | User can't delete others' data |
| Rate limited | `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` | Too many requests |
| Server error | `INTERNAL` | Database connection failed |
| Timeout | `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` | RPC took too long |
| Unimplemented | `UNIMPLEMENTED` | Feature not yet available |

### Rich Error Details

For complex errors, include structured details:

```proto
message ErrorDetails {
  string error_code = 1;        // Machine-readable: "INVALID_EMAIL"
  string message = 2;           // Human-readable
  optional google.protobuf.Struct context = 3;  // Additional metadata
}

message CreateUserResponse {
  string user_id = 1;
}
// If validation fails, server returns:
// Status: INVALID_ARGUMENT
// Message: "Validation failed"
// Details: { error_code: "INVALID_EMAIL", context: { field: "email" } }
```

## Streaming

### Server Streaming (Server Pushes Multiple)

Use for long-running operations, log output, or subscriptions:

```proto
service BuildService {
  rpc Build(BuildRequest) returns (stream BuildOutput);
}

message BuildRequest {
  string project_id = 1;
  bool release = 2;
}

message BuildOutput {
  string line = 1;
  StreamType stream_type = 2;  // STDOUT, STDERR, PROGRESS
  bool is_final = 3;
  int32 exit_code = 4;         // Only set when is_final=true
  int64 duration_ms = 5;       // Only set when is_final=true
}

enum StreamType {
  STREAM_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  STREAM_TYPE_STDOUT = 1;
  STREAM_TYPE_STDERR = 2;
  STREAM_TYPE_PROGRESS = 3;
  STREAM_TYPE_RESULT = 4;
}
```

### Client Streaming (Client Pushes Multiple)

Use for bulk uploads or accumulating state:

```proto
service DataService {
  rpc UploadBatch(stream DataChunk) returns (UploadResult);
}

message DataChunk {
  string batch_id = 1;
  bytes data = 2;
  bool is_final = 3;
}

message UploadResult {
  int32 chunks_received = 1;
  int64 bytes_received = 2;
}
```

### Bidirectional Streaming (Both Sides Push)

Use for interactive sessions:

```proto
service ChatService {
  rpc SendChat(stream ChatMessage) returns (stream ChatMessage);
}

message ChatMessage {
  string session_id = 1;
  string content = 2;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp timestamp = 3;
}
```

## Backwards Compatibility

### Adding Fields

Proto3 is forward/backward compatible by default:

```proto
// v1.0
message Order {
  string order_id = 1;
  string customer_id = 2;
}

// v1.1 - Add new field
message Order {
  string order_id = 1;
  string customer_id = 2;
  optional string notes = 3;  // New field, safe to add
}
```

### Deprecating Fields

Use `deprecated = true`:

```proto
message Order {
  string order_id = 1;
  string customer_id = 2;
  string old_status = 3 [deprecated = true];  // Clients ignore
  OrderStatus new_status = 4;
}

enum OrderStatus {
  ORDER_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  ORDER_STATUS_PENDING = 1;
  reserved 2;  // removed: ORDER_STATUS_SHIPPED
}
```

### Removing RPCs

Don't delete old RPCs; deprecate them:

```proto
service OrderService {
  rpc GetOrderLegacy(GetOrderRequest) returns (OrderLegacy) {
    deprecated: true;
  }
  
  rpc GetOrder(GetOrderRequest) returns (Order);
}
```

## Documentation

Add comments to all public surfaces:

```proto
service OrderService {
  // Creates a new order and returns the created resource.
  // Returns ALREADY_EXISTS if order with that ID exists.
  rpc CreateOrder(CreateOrderRequest) returns (Order);
}

message Order {
  // Unique order identifier, immutable.
  string order_id = 1;
  
  // Customer who placed the order.
  string customer_id = 2;
  
  // ISO 8601 timestamp when order was created.
  google.protobuf.Timestamp created_at = 3;
}

enum OrderStatus {
  // Status not specified.
  ORDER_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  
  // Order received, awaiting processing.
  ORDER_STATUS_PENDING = 1;
}
```

## File Organization

```
proto/
├── common.proto                 # Shared messages, enums
├── errors.proto                 # Error details
├── STYLE_GUIDE.md              # This file
├── REFACTORING_CHECKLIST.md    # Tracking migration
├── orders/
│   ├── order.proto             # Order entity
│   ├── service.proto           # Order service
│   └── events.proto            # Order events
└── users/
    ├── user.proto              # User entity
    ├── service.proto           # User service
    └── auth.proto              # Authentication
```

**Pattern:** One top-level entity per file for maintainability.

## Refactoring Checklist

When updating a proto file:

- [ ] Replace `string "json"` fields with `google.protobuf.Struct`
- [ ] Replace `string` enums with `enum` types
- [ ] Remove `success: bool` fields from responses
- [ ] Ensure enum first value is `_UNSPECIFIED = 0`
- [ ] Add `optional` keyword to nullable fields
- [ ] Reserve deleted field numbers
- [ ] Import common types from `common.proto`
- [ ] Add comments to all public messages/services
- [ ] Verify RPC method names follow conventions
- [ ] Run `protoc` with generated code (check for breaking changes)

## Example: Complete Refactor

### Before

```proto
syntax = "proto3";
package users;

service UserService {
  rpc CreateUser(CreateUserRequest) returns (CreateUserResponse);
}

message CreateUserRequest {
  string username = 1;
  string email = 2;
  string metadata_json = 3;
}

message CreateUserResponse {
  bool success = 1;
  string user_id = 2;
  string status = 3;  // "active", "pending"
  string error = 4;
}
```

### After

```proto
syntax = "proto3";

package users.v1;

import "google/protobuf/struct.proto";
import "common.proto";

service UserService {
  // Creates a new user and returns the created resource.
  rpc CreateUser(CreateUserRequest) returns (User);
}

message User {
  string user_id = 1;
  string username = 2;
  string email = 3;
  UserStatus status = 4;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp created_at = 5;
  optional google.protobuf.Struct metadata = 6;
}

message CreateUserRequest {
  string username = 1;
  string email = 2;
  optional google.protobuf.Struct metadata = 3;
}

enum UserStatus {
  USER_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  USER_STATUS_ACTIVE = 1;
  USER_STATUS_PENDING = 2;
}
```

ASSISTANT: You're right to push back. I overstated it, and the reason it renders is the thing I should have checked first.

## The correction

I claimed the contract drift was broadly breaking. It isn't. Sorted by message, all 9 colliding messages in `operation.proto` are on the **write/action path**:

`BatchMutateResponse`, `CallMethodResponse`, `MutateResponse`, `SetPropertyResponse`, `OvsdbTransactResponse`, `dbusCallResponse`, `DbusGetPropertyResponse`, `GetSchemaResponse`, `VerifyChainResponse`

And the messages your render path actually consumes, `ListPluginsResponse` and `GetStateResponse`, are **clean**. Identical field numbering on both sides. That is why the browser looks fine. The dashboard paints itself from list/state reads, and those decode correctly.

## Two things I got wrong about the mechanism

**1. Proto3 omits default scalars.** In `CallMethodResponse`, odbus has `bool success = 1`. When `success` is `false`, field 1 is *not on the wire at all*. So the UI's `result` at field 1 just stays undefined and you get an empty render, not a crash. A mismatch only materialises when `success == true`, i.e. only on a *successful* mutation. That is why casual browsing never trips it.

**2. Not every collision is a wire-type conflict.** I lumped them together. They fail in two different ways:

| kind | example | wire types | behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| shifted by deleted `success` | `CallMethodResponse` #2 `Value result` vs UI `uint64 event_id` | 2 vs 0 | tag mismatch, decode error or skip |
| retyped in place | `GetSchemaResponse` #1 `string schema_json` vs UI `Struct schema` | 2 vs 2 | **wire types match**, so it decodes "successfully" and silently produces garbage |

That second row is the more insidious one, and it is not a crash at all. `string` and `Struct` are both length-delimited, so protobuf-ts happily reads the JSON text bytes and tries to parse them as a `Struct`. You get an empty or nonsense schema, no error.

Same class: `string container_type` to `ContainerType` in `privacy_network.proto` is string vs enum, which *is* a real wire-type conflict (2 vs 0), so that one does break.

## What I verified vs what I inferred

Verified:
- Running binary `/usr/local/bin/op-grpc-bridge`, Aug 2 03:49, built *after* the Aug 1 21:18 proto rewrite.
- Its embedded reflection descriptor literally contains `CallMethodResponse` then `success`, `result`, `event_id`, `event_hash`, `error`. So the live server is on the new shape.
- Transport is binary `application/grpc-web+proto` (`src/grpc/client.ts:295`), so names do not matter, only numbers.
- The UI does wire up the affected calls: `callMethod`, `mutate`, `setProperty` at `src/grpc/client.ts`, plus 5 `verifyChain` and 9 `getSchema` sites.

Not verified: I could not complete a live write-path call. `127.0.0.1:8090` returned `grpc-status: 16` UNAUTHENTICATED, and I did not go looking for your credentials. So the runtime consequence on the write path is read off the descriptors, not observed.

## The honest version of the finding

The drift is real and the live server genuinely disagrees with the UI's protos, but it is **latent, not active**. It is scoped to mutations, plugin method invocation, OVSDB transact, chain verification, and schema fetch. Reads are fine, which is 100% of what you see when you load a page.

The single testable prediction: **invoke a plugin method that succeeds** and the result should come back empty or malformed rather than correct, because that is the only moment `success = true` puts a varint in field 1. If you have an Invoke page action handy, that is a 30-second check and it either confirms or kills the whole thesis.

This workspace does **not** hand-write per-plugin `.proto` files. Proto generation is
automatic, driven entirely by each plugin's `PluginSchema`. If you remember one thing

## The real pipeline (roll → seal → freeze → hot)

```
1. Plugin declares  → PluginSchema { methods: HashMap<String, MethodDecl>, signals: Vec<SignalDecl>, ... }
                       in crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<plugin>.rs
2. Schema gets put   → op-projection's SchemaEngine publishes the catalog hash
                       (op_identity::schema_bridge::schema_catalog_hash())
3. Sealed by blob    → op-blob seals the plugin object into an immutable blob:
                       /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob
                       (op-blob is the ONLY writer — never write blobs elsewhere)
4. Descriptors       → TWO separate reflection layers exist, don't confuse them:
   for reflection       a) STATIC: crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs generates
                            plugin_methods.proto from every plugin's schema.methods,
                            compiles it with tonic_build into operation_descriptor.bin
                            (a protobuf FileDescriptorSet), served by tonic-reflection.
                         b) DYNAMIC: crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/dynamic_reflection.rs
                            (ActiveReflectionCatalog) hydrates live from the sealed
                            SHM blob catalog via hydrate_reflection_from_shm() —
                            this is the "frozen" descriptor set for what's actually
                            present right now, independent of what's compiled in.
5. Frozen            → the blob + its descriptors are immutable once sealed.
6. gRPC socket = hot → crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs registers the
                       generated per-plugin service (plugin_method_routes.rs,
                       add_routes()) on the tonic UDS bridge, dispatching each
                       RPC to call_generated_plugin_method_typed(plugin_id,
                       schema_name, ...) which routes through PluginService.CallMethod
                       — i.e. gRPC never bypasses D-Bus, it's a bridge, not a
                       second control plane.
```

## The Auto-Creator Plugin (an ongoing capability, not a one-off batch)

This is **not** a one-time task to fix ~11 named plugins. It's a standing
system capability: whenever the system encounters *any* missing plugin —
now, or a new one added in the future — it automatically generates that
plugin and submits it for **human review**, never auto-merges/auto-seals it
unreviewed. The current ~11 gaps are just the first real instances that
exercise this, not the scope.

Consistent with this workspace's "reactive, not polled" principle (CLAUDE.md):
this should be triggered by an actual arrival/lookup that reveals the gap
(e.g. a D-Bus/gRPC call or reflection lookup against a plugin whose
`schema.methods` is empty, or a plugin name that doesn't resolve at all),
not a cron-style sweep re-scanning all plugins on a timer.

Build it as a plugin itself (same `PluginSchema`/`MethodDecl` pattern as every
plugin in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`), whose job is to:

1. **Detect a gap on encounter** — when something references a plugin that's
   missing or has `schema.methods.is_empty()` (same emptiness check
   `build.rs::collect_plugin_methods` already uses to skip plugins), that's
   the trigger — not a periodic scan of the whole registry.
2. **Research that specific gap** — drive deep research via the **NotebookLM
   MCP** (once wired up) to determine what capabilities/operations the
   missing plugin should realistically expose, given its existing state
   struct (if any), documentation, and prior art from comparable plugins
   already in the registry. This replaces guessing or generic Get/List/Watch
   stubs with a grounded, plugin-specific proposal.
3. **Synthesize typed schemas** — turn the research output into real Rust
   input/output structs (`#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]`) and `MethodDecl`
   entries — per the "no `AckOutput`" rule above, every synthesized method
   needs its own meaningful typed request/response, not a generic ack.
4. **Submit for human review — do not auto-apply.** The output is a proposed
   plugin/schema (e.g. a diff/PR against `<name>_schema()`, or a new
   `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs` for a wholly new plugin),
   held for a human to approve before it's merged. Only after human approval

   blob → hot). The auto-creator must never seal a blob or register a plugin
   into the live catalog on its own. It never emits `.proto` directly and
   never writes to `/proto/plugin_methods/` — the single source of truth
   stays `schema.methods`, authored by a human-approved change.

## JSON Schema → proto type mapping (what `build.rs` actually does)

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs::json_schema_type_to_proto` maps:

| JSON Schema | Proto type |
|---|---|
| `string` (or has non-empty `enum`) | `string` |
| `boolean` | `bool` |
| `integer` | `int64` |
| `number` | `double` |
| `array` | `repeated <item type>` |
| `object` with `properties` | `google.protobuf.Struct` |
| anything else / untyped | `google.protobuf.Value` |

Field numbers are **not** sequential — they're an FNV-1a hash of the field name
(`stable_field_number`), deliberately stable across regenerations rather than
assignment-order-stable. This is intentional in this codebase (schemas are
generated from Rust structs whose field order can shift); don't "fix" it to
sequential numbering without checking with the user first, since wire
compatibility here depends on the hash being stable, not on classic proto
field-number discipline.

## Known project-specific tensions vs. generic gRPC best practice

Be aware of these before applying textbook advice unmodified:

- **Do not use `AckOutput { success: bool }` for new/generated methods.**
  It exists in the codebase (see `proxy_server.rs`) as a legacy shortcut for
  "no meaningful return value," but every method a plugin exposes should have
  a real, dedicated typed **input** struct and typed **output** struct that
  reflect what the operation actually consumes and returns — not a generic
  bool. This matters especially for the auto-creator (below): when it
  synthesizes methods for a previously-empty plugin, it must generate a
  specific `<Method>Input` and `<Method>Output` schemars struct per method,
  never fall back to `AckOutput`. Errors still go through `tonic::Status` /
  D-Bus error replies, never a `success: false` field.
- **Enums are flattened to `string`, not real proto `enum`.** JSON Schema
  `enum` currently maps to proto `string` (see table above), so the classic
  `FOO_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0` convention isn't applied by the generator today.
  If asked to add real proto enums, that requires changing
  `json_schema_type_to_proto` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs`, not just the
  plugin schema.
- **No streaming (`Watch`) support in the generator.** Every generated RPC is
  unary (`rpc X(Request) returns (Response)`); `stream` responses aren't
  emitted by `generate_plugin_methods_proto`. A real `Watch`/streaming RPC for
  a plugin needs a hand-written service in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/`, not
  a `MethodDecl`.
- **One generated file per bridge crate**, not the "1-1-1" file-per-message
  convention — `plugin_methods.proto` bundles every plugin's messages/services
  in one generated file. That's fine; it's a build artifact, not hand-maintained
  source, so the usual "small modular .proto files" guidance doesn't apply to it.

## Generic protobuf/gRPC conventions (still apply to hand-written `.proto`)

For any `.proto` you *do* hand-write (domain services under
`crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/`, not plugin-derived ones):

- `snake_case` field names, `CamelCase` message/service/RPC names, package names
  lowercase (this repo uses `operation.plugin.v1`-style packages).
- Reserve field numbers for removed fields; never reuse them.
- Prefer `optional` for fields that may be absent; avoid letting one field's
  value change the semantic meaning of another.
- Real proto `enum`s (where you control the generator, e.g. hand-written
  services) always start with `..._UNSPECIFIED = 0`.
- Use gRPC status codes (`tonic::Status`) for error paths; reserve response
  message fields for actual data.
- TLS is mandatory in this workspace (per CLAUDE.md zero-trust transport) —
  never wire a new gRPC service as plaintext, even over UDS.
- Server reflection (`tonic-reflection`) must stay wired for every new service
  so it's discoverable by `op-cognitive-mcp` and the gRPC diagnostic page —
  don't add a service that bypasses reflection registration.

## Quick diagnostic checklist

If a plugin isn't showing up / isn't callable over gRPC:

1. Does `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs`'s `<name>_schema()`
   actually populate `schema.methods`? (Empty → `build.rs` skips it entirely.)
2. Is the plugin registered via `inventory::submit! { PluginReg::new(...) }` in
   its own file (self-registration — check `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`
   only if the plugin doesn't show up in `available_plugins()` at all)?
3. Did `cargo build -p op-grpc-bridge` actually rerun? (`build.rs` only reruns on
   changes under `../op-plugins/src/state_plugins` or `build.rs` itself.)
4. Is the plugin actually **sealed** in the SHM blob catalog
   (`/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/`)? Static compiled-in proto support and the
   *dynamic* "hot" reflection/routing are two different gates — a plugin can
   compile fine and still be invisible if it was never sealed.

fn stable_field_number(name: &str) -> i32 {
    const FNV_OFFSET: u32 = 0x811c9dc5;
    const FNV_PRIME: u32 = 0x01000193;
    const MAX_FIELD: u32 = 536_870_911;
    const RESERVED_START: u32 = 19_000;
    const RESERVED_END: u32 = 19_999;

    let mut hash = FNV_OFFSET;
    for byte in name.as_bytes() {
        hash ^= u32::from(*byte);
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(FNV_PRIME);
    }

    let mut number = (hash % MAX_FIELD).max(1);
    if (RESERVED_START..=RESERVED_END).contains(&number) {
        number += RESERVED_END - RESERVED_START + 1;
    }
    number as i32
}

<skill name="grpc-expert" filePath="/home/jeremy/.agents/skills/grpc-expert/SKILL.md">
# gRPC Expert — OP-DBUS

This workspace does **not** hand-write per-plugin `.proto` files. Proto generation is
automatic, driven entirely by each plugin's `PluginSchema`. If you remember one thing
from this skill: **fixing a plugin's gRPC surface means editing its Rust schema
function, not writing `.proto`.**

## The real pipeline (roll → seal → freeze → hot)

```
1. Plugin declares  → PluginSchema { methods: HashMap<String, MethodDecl>, signals: Vec<SignalDecl>, ... }
                       in crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<plugin>.rs
2. Schema gets put   → op-projection's SchemaEngine publishes the catalog hash
                       (op_identity::schema_bridge::schema_catalog_hash())
3. Sealed by blob    → op-blob seals the plugin object into an immutable blob:
                       /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob
                       (op-blob is the ONLY writer — never write blobs elsewhere)
4. Descriptors       → TWO separate reflection layers exist, don't confuse them:
   for reflection       a) STATIC: crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs generates
                            plugin_methods.proto from every plugin's schema.methods,
                            compiles it with tonic_build into operation_descriptor.bin
                            (a protobuf FileDescriptorSet), served by tonic-reflection.
                         b) DYNAMIC: crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/dynamic_reflection.rs
                            (ActiveReflectionCatalog) hydrates live from the sealed
                            SHM blob catalog via hydrate_reflection_from_shm() —
                            this is the "frozen" descriptor set for what's actually
                            present right now, independent of what's compiled in.
5. Frozen            → the blob + its descriptors are immutable once sealed.
6. gRPC socket = hot → crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs registers the
                       generated per-plugin service (plugin_method_routes.rs,
                       add_routes()) on the tonic UDS bridge, dispatching each
                       RPC to call_generated_plugin_method_typed(plugin_id,
                       schema_name, ...) which routes through PluginService.CallMethod
                       — i.e. gRPC never bypasses D-Bus, it's a bridge, not a
                       second control plane.
```

A plugin shows green/connected on the gRPC diagnostic page **iff**:
- its `PluginSchema.methods` is non-empty (empty → `build.rs` silently skips it —
  see `collect_plugin_methods()`), **and**
- the plugin is sealed in the SHM blob catalog.

## Where to actually make changes

| Task | File |
|---|---|
| Add/fix methods for plugin `<name>` | `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs`, inside `<name>_schema()` |
| Reusable input/output builders | `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs` |
| Regenerate the derived `.proto` + routes | Just rebuild — `build.rs` regenerates on every `cargo build -p op-grpc-bridge` (it `rerun-if-changed`s `../op-plugins/src/state_plugins`) |
| Wire a genuinely new (non-plugin-derived) service | `crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/*.proto`, add to the `compile_protos` list + `rerun-if-changed` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs`, then register in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs` |
| Inspect what's currently generated | `target/{debug,release}/build/op-grpc-bridge-*/out/plugin_methods.proto` (build artifact — never hand-edit) |

**Never** create files under a `/proto/plugin_methods/` directory or a
`plugin_methods_unified.proto` by hand — those paths don't exist in this repo and
aren't part of the real pipeline; that was a stale spec from an earlier session.
The single source of truth is `schema.methods`.

## Adding methods to a plugin (the actual workflow)

Look at `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/proxy_server.rs` (`proxy_server_schema()`)
for the canonical pattern:

```rust
use op_state_store::{MethodDecl, PluginSchema, SideEffect};

schema.methods.insert(
    "start_proxy".to_string(),
    method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<StartProxyInput, plugin_scaffold_helpers::AckOutput>(
        "start_proxy",
        SideEffect::Mutation,       // Read | Mutation
        false,                       // idempotent?
        "cap.network.proxy.start@v1",   // required_capability
        "mut.network.proxy.start@v1",   // subid — must follow the taxonomy in CLAUDE.md
    ),
);
```

- Define `StartProxyInput` (and a typed output struct, or reuse `AckOutput`) as
  `#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]` structs — the JSON Schema is derived, never
  hand-written as `serde_json::json!({...})` unless there's no existing helper.
- `method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<Input, Output>` is the current
  (non-deprecated) helper; the single-generic `method_decl_from_schemars` is
  deprecated but still present for legacy callers.
- `subid` must be registered in the canonical registry per CLAUDE.md
  (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs`) — CI enforces
  uniqueness.
- For plugins with **zero** declared methods today (the ones missing from the
  diagnostic page), don't hand-author their methods one by one — see
  **The Auto-Creator Plugin** below. That's the actual deliverable: a plugin
  that finds these gaps and fills them itself, using real research per plugin.

## The Auto-Creator Plugin (an ongoing capability, not a one-off batch)

This is **not** a one-time task to fix ~11 named plugins. It's a standing
system capability: whenever the system encounters *any* missing plugin —
now, or a new one added in the future — it automatically generates that
plugin and submits it for **human review**, never auto-merges/auto-seals it
unreviewed. The current ~11 gaps are just the first real instances that
exercise this, not the scope.

Consistent with this workspace's "reactive, not polled" principle (CLAUDE.md):
this should be triggered by an actual arrival/lookup that reveals the gap
(e.g. a D-Bus/gRPC call or reflection lookup against a plugin whose
`schema.methods` is empty, or a plugin name that doesn't resolve at all),
not a cron-style sweep re-scanning all plugins on a timer.

Build it as a plugin itself (same `PluginSchema`/`MethodDecl` pattern as every
plugin in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`), whose job is to:

1. **Detect a gap on encounter** — when something references a plugin that's
   missing or has `schema.methods.is_empty()` (same emptiness check
   `build.rs::collect_plugin_methods` already uses to skip plugins), that's
   the trigger — not a periodic scan of the whole registry.
2. **Research that specific gap** — drive deep research via the **NotebookLM
   MCP** (once wired up) to determine what capabilities/operations the
   missing plugin should realistically expose, given its existing state
   struct (if any), documentation, and prior art from comparable plugins
   already in the registry. This replaces guessing or generic Get/List/Watch
   stubs with a grounded, plugin-specific proposal.
3. **Synthesize typed schemas** — turn the research output into real Rust
   input/output structs (`#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]`) and `MethodDecl`
   entries — per the "no `AckOutput`" rule above, every synthesized method
   needs its own meaningful typed request/response, not a generic ack.
4. **Submit for human review — do not auto-apply.** The output is a proposed
   plugin/schema (e.g. a diff/PR against `<name>_schema()`, or a new
   `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs` for a wholly new plugin),
   held for a human to approve before it's merged. Only after human approval
   does it enter the normal pipeline (build → proto → reflection → sealed
   blob → hot). The auto-creator must never seal a blob or register a plugin
   into the live catalog on its own. It never emits `.proto` directly and
   never writes to `/proto/plugin_methods/` — the single source of truth
   stays `schema.methods`, authored by a human-approved change.

In short: this is a **standing, reactive meta-plugin that drafts schemas for
whatever plugin is found missing, research-backed via NotebookLM, gated by
human review** — not a fixed batch job for a specific list of plugins.

## JSON Schema → proto type mapping (what `build.rs` actually does)

`crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs::json_schema_type_to_proto` maps:

| JSON Schema | Proto type |
|---|---|
| `string` (or has non-empty `enum`) | `string` |
| `boolean` | `bool` |
| `integer` | `int64` |
| `number` | `double` |
| `array` | `repeated <item type>` |
| `object` with `properties` | `google.protobuf.Struct` |
| anything else / untyped | `google.protobuf.Value` |

Field numbers are **not** sequential — they're an FNV-1a hash of the field name
(`stable_field_number`), deliberately stable across regenerations rather than
assignment-order-stable. This is intentional in this codebase (schemas are
generated from Rust structs whose field order can shift); don't "fix" it to
sequential numbering without checking with the user first, since wire
compatibility here depends on the hash being stable, not on classic proto
field-number discipline.

## Known project-specific tensions vs. generic gRPC best practice

Be aware of these before applying textbook advice unmodified:

- **Do not use `AckOutput { success: bool }` for new/generated methods.**
  It exists in the codebase (see `proxy_server.rs`) as a legacy shortcut for
  "no meaningful return value," but every method a plugin exposes should have
  a real, dedicated typed **input** struct and typed **output** struct that
  reflect what the operation actually consumes and returns — not a generic
  bool. This matters especially for the auto-creator (below): when it
  synthesizes methods for a previously-empty plugin, it must generate a
  specific `<Method>Input` and `<Method>Output` schemars struct per method,
  never fall back to `AckOutput`. Errors still go through `tonic::Status` /
  D-Bus error replies, never a `success: false` field.
- **Enums are flattened to `string`, not real proto `enum`.** JSON Schema
  `enum` currently maps to proto `string` (see table above), so the classic
  `FOO_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0` convention isn't applied by the generator today.
  If asked to add real proto enums, that requires changing
  `json_schema_type_to_proto` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs`, not just the
  plugin schema.
- **No streaming (`Watch`) support in the generator.** Every generated RPC is
  unary (`rpc X(Request) returns (Response)`); `stream` responses aren't
  emitted by `generate_plugin_methods_proto`. A real `Watch`/streaming RPC for
  a plugin needs a hand-written service in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/`, not
  a `MethodDecl`.
- **One generated file per bridge crate**, not the "1-1-1" file-per-message
  convention — `plugin_methods.proto` bundles every plugin's messages/services
  in one generated file. That's fine; it's a build artifact, not hand-maintained
  source, so the usual "small modular .proto files" guidance doesn't apply to it.

## Generic protobuf/gRPC conventions (still apply to hand-written `.proto`)

For any `.proto` you *do* hand-write (domain services under
`crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/`, not plugin-derived ones):

- `snake_case` field names, `CamelCase` message/service/RPC names, package names
  lowercase (this repo uses `operation.plugin.v1`-style packages).
- Reserve field numbers for removed fields; never reuse them.
- Prefer `optional` for fields that may be absent; avoid letting one field's
  value change the semantic meaning of another.
- Real proto `enum`s (where you control the generator, e.g. hand-written
  services) always start with `..._UNSPECIFIED = 0`.
- Use gRPC status codes (`tonic::Status`) for error paths; reserve response
  message fields for actual data.
- TLS is mandatory in this workspace (per CLAUDE.md zero-trust transport) —
  never wire a new gRPC service as plaintext, even over UDS.
- Server reflection (`tonic-reflection`) must stay wired for every new service
  so it's discoverable by `op-cognitive-mcp` and the gRPC diagnostic page —
  don't add a service that bypasses reflection registration.

## Quick diagnostic checklist

If a plugin isn't showing up / isn't callable over gRPC:

1. Does `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs`'s `<name>_schema()`
   actually populate `schema.methods`? (Empty → `build.rs` skips it entirely.)
2. Is the plugin registered via `inventory::submit! { PluginReg::new(...) }` in
   its own file (self-registration — check `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`
   only if the plugin doesn't show up in `available_plugins()` at all)?
3. Did `cargo build -p op-grpc-bridge` actually rerun? (`build.rs` only reruns on
   changes under `../op-plugins/src/state_plugins` or `build.rs` itself.)
4. Is the plugin actually **sealed** in the SHM blob catalog
   (`/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/`)? Static compiled-in proto support and the
   *dynamic* "hot" reflection/routing are two different gates — a plugin can
   compile fine and still be invisible if it was never sealed.
